notes: The light everything reads from one sun (simcore/light.hpp): the sun's elevation at the scenario's place, date and hour (simcore/solar.hpp, meeus_1998) against these thresholds. Day with the sun at low_sun_deg or higher; night more than twilight_deg below the horizon; dawn or dusk between, by whether it rises. The TV sight has daylight down to tv_min_elevation_deg; the battery is dark (lamp signals, the night march, the guns' optical sights blind, the waves' night factor) below optical_night_deg. twilight_deg must equal visual_range.json's (test_light.cpp). Roadmap S8: the light on the ground in lux (the sun's clear sky by its elevation, brown_1952, and the moon by its phase and height, krisciunas_schaefer_1991); the TV's contrast threshold times the square root of tv_full_lux over that light when it is less (rose_1948), so the TV's range falls through the twilight before its daylight ends at tv_min_elevation_deg; the moon's share of the night 0 at moonless_lux and 1 at full_moon_lux, logarithmic between (the eye's range at night, visual_range.json's moonlit_m). The air war reads this file too (its theatre's parts of the day, roadmap S8).
source: derived: civil twilight's 6 degrees is the astronomical definition (meeus_1998); the light in lux brown_1952 and krisciunas_schaefer_1991; the others game values

twilight_deg.source: derived: civil twilight, the sun up to 6 degrees below the horizon (the astronomical definition)

low_sun_deg.source: game value: the sun this high or higher is full day; below it, the long shadows and glare of dawn or dusk

tv_min_elevation_deg.source: derived: the end of civil twilight (the astronomical definition), the light a daylight TV camera of the period still works in (simcore/solar.hpp's note)

optical_night_deg.source: derived: the end of civil twilight (the astronomical definition): below it the battery works by night (lamps, the night march, optical sights blind)

tv_full_lux.source: game value: the light on the ground at sunset (about 400 lux, brown_1952) taken as the least a daylight TV camera of the period works in at its full contrast threshold; below it the threshold rises as the square root of the light's fall (rose_1948)

moonless_lux.source: brown_1952: a clear moonless night's light on the ground (starlight and airglow), about a thousandth of a lux

full_moon_lux.source: krisciunas_schaefer_1991: a full moon high in a clear sky gives about a quarter of a lux on level ground (simcore/light.hpp MoonLux)
